title: Bondum Dogon
text: Bondum Dogon, also known as Bondum Dom or Najamba-Kindige, is a Dogon language spoken by approximately 24,700 people in the central Mopti region of Mali, particularly around Douentza town and in villages such as Kubewel, Adia, and along the highway to the west.

title: Dogon languages - Wikiwand
text: The Dogon languages are a small closely related language family that is spoken by the Dogon people of Mali and may belong to the proposed Niger–Congo family. There are about 600,000 speakers of its dozen languages.North Plateau Dogon. Dogul Dom Dogon. Yanda-Bondum-Tebul.

title: SONGHAY AND DOGON. : languagehat.com
text: Hausa nama “meat” looks pretty Niger-Congo-ish (cf Kusaal nim “meat”), for example. Mind you, Hausa is a magpie language, like English, forever stealing other people’s words. Even the Hausa word for “two”, biyu, seems not to be Chadic, but borrowed from some Niger-Congo language.
